To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the atomic form factor for x-ray absorption in a crystal is a function of the angle between the direction of the incident x-ray beam and the normal to the crystal surface; 2) the anomalous absorption effect is greater at larger x-ray scattering angles; and 3) the atomic form factors are not as steep on the short-wavelength side of an absorption edge as the theory predicts.
the atomic form factor for X-rays near the K-absorption edge of a crystal is a function of both the scattering angle and the energy of the incident X-rays.
The anomalous dispersion of the atomic scattering factor for X-rays near an absorption edge can be calculated theoretically for a finite scattering angle.

the anomalous dispersion of the X-ray atomic scattering factor is the main cause of the anomalous X-ray diffraction.
